title: Adaptive prefill/decode circuit-breaker that uses kernel backpressure and attention-cost signals
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: Reduce latency tail and avoid catastrophic throughput collapses during transient kernel contention by adding an adaptive circuit-breaker into the prefill/decode allocator. The breaker will ingest runtime signals from kernel selection heuristics and attention-cost estimators (sparsity and KV cache hit rate) and decide when to split phases, temporarily demote noncritical tenants, or enable speculative hedging. This ticket covers design, simulator validation, a staged experiment, and a conservative rollout path for Hosted and Dedicated fleets.

Background: We observe intermittent 95th-99th pct latency spikes when large prefill batches push heavy attention kernels (dense long-seq attention) into a small set of devices. Current fairness heuristics compensate by token-weighted allocation but do not react quickly to kernel-level backpressure. A circuit-breaker that reasons at kernel-cost granularity can stop overloaded kernels from accepting new slices and redirect short-latency-prefill traffic to lighter kernels or smaller phase splits.

Non-goal: This is not a new long-term scheduler replacement or a tenant billing policy change. It is a runtime mitigation layer layered on top of existing arbitrators to reduce tail latency during transient kernel hotspots.
acceptance_criteria: Simulator shows >=20% reduction in 95th latency for workload mix A under synthetic kernel-hotspot scenario
No >1% throughput regression on steady-state medium-load tests
Experiment monitors (latency, kernel queue length, KV hit rate) show expected breaker state transitions and stable recovery during injected overloads
Documentation of breaker config knobs and safe defaults merged to ops runbook
design_notes: Input signals: per-kernel queue depth, per-kernel estimated per-token compute cost, attention-density estimator (top-k attention mass), KV cache hit ratio, tenant soft-priority score, and recent phase-split frequency
Decision outputs: allow/deny new slices on a kernel, force phase-split (prefill -> smaller microphases), steer to lighter kernel variant, or enable short hedged decode on background model variant
Policy: multiplier-based soft-circuit with hysteresis (open probability, cooldown window, progressive demotion tiers) rather than binary open/closed to avoid oscillation

Fairness consideration: maintain tenant-level soft credits; when demotion occurs prefer tenants that exceed credit or are best-effort class. Provide opt-out tag for enterprise customers with SLA-backed reserved capacity
Kernel cost estimation: combine static profiling (model, seq_len) and online probe samples; fall back to conservative estimate if missing
Observability: expose breaker state per-kernel, per-host, and per-tenant for dashboarding and alerting
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Add lightweight breaker controller in allocator with read-only kernel signals and no enforcement (telemetry-only). Instrument state metrics and create dashboard panels.

Phase 2: Implement probabilistic soft-circuit enforcement for prefill admission; add API flags to enable steering to alternate kernels (quantized variants) and to request microphase split hint from downstream executor.
Phase 3: Add tenant soft-credit ledger integration and demotion policy; add config-driven hysteresis and cooldowns; add unit/integration tests in runtime simulator.
Phase 4: Canary rollout to low-risk region and Dedicated dev pool; monitor, iterate, and expand to wider fleet behind feature flag
experiments: Simulator scenario: 30% heavy long-prefill synthetic (seq_len 2048) injected for 60s while baseline steady traffic runs; compare baseline vs breaker-on
A/B canary: 5% of production routing to breaker-on for two hours; automatic rollback if 95p latency increases or error rate rises
Kernel-demotion calibration: sweep demotion thresholds to find knee where latency improves without excessive throughput loss
metrics: 95th/99th latency (prefill and decode) by tenant class
Per-kernel queue length and processing rate
KV cache hit ratio and correlation with phase splits
Breaker activation count, average open duration, and rollback events
Customer error rate and tail failure mode counts
rollout_plan: Small canary (5% traffic) for 48 hours with auto-rollback triggers
Gradual ramp (5% -> 25% -> 60% -> 100%) over two weeks with monitoring windows
Hold at each step until SLO pass for 2 hours; require sign-off from runtime-owners before next step
Dedicated capacity: default off; enable by request after testing
testing_notes: Add deterministic unit tests for hysteresis state machine with synthetic timers
Integration tests: run allocator + executor in local cluster to verify steering and microphase hints propagate correctly
Chaos test: inject delayed kernel responses and ensure breaker recovers cleanly without starvation
Performance test: ensure breaker controller CPU overhead <2% per host at 1k QPS
